Eligibility traces

The λ-return of Lesson 57 looks forward, so it has to wait for the future. An eligibility trace looks backward instead: each state leaves a footprint that fades by $\gamma\lambda$ per step. When a TD error arrives, every state with a footprint is updated in proportion to it. This is TD(λ), and it learns on every step.

TD(λ) on the 19-state walk

Online TD(λ) with accumulating traces, measured as in Lessons 56 and 57 (RMS error over the first 10 episodes, 30 runs).

For small $\alpha$ the curves match Lesson 57's λ-return figure: TD(λ) approximates the λ-return. At large $\alpha$ and large $\lambda$ it does worse, because a state visited several times gets several large updates within one episode.

The maths

TD(λ) keeps a trace vector $\mathbf{z}_t$, the same size as the weights $\mathbf{w}$, starting at $\mathbf{z}_{-1} = \mathbf{0}$ each episode. On every step:

$$\begin{aligned} \mathbf{z}_t &= \gamma\lambda\, \mathbf{z}_{t-1} + \nabla \hat v(S_t, \mathbf{w}_t) \\ \delta_t &= R_{t+1} + \gamma\, \hat v(S_{t+1}, \mathbf{w}_t) - \hat v(S_t, \mathbf{w}_t) \\ \mathbf{w}_{t+1} &= \mathbf{w}_t + \alpha\, \delta_t\, \mathbf{z}_t \end{aligned}$$

The trace fades by $\gamma\lambda$ each step, then grows by the gradient of the current estimate: the weights that produced $\hat v(S_t, \mathbf{w}_t)$ get credit. Then one TD error (Lesson 46) updates every component in proportion to its trace.

In a table, $\hat v(s, \mathbf{w}) = V(s)$ and the gradient is 1 for the current state and 0 elsewhere. So each state has its own trace:

$$z_t(s) = \gamma\lambda\, z_{t-1}(s) + \mathbb{1}[S_t = s], \qquad V(s) \leftarrow V(s) + \alpha\, \delta_t\, z_t(s) \ \text{ for all } s$$

Unrolled, $z_t(s) = \sum_{k \le t,\ S_k = s} (\gamma\lambda)^{t-k}$: a sum of fading footprints, one per visit. A replacing trace sets $z_t(S_t) = 1$ instead of adding 1, so it never exceeds 1.

Why this matches Lesson 57. Suppose $V$ is held fixed during an episode and the updates are added up at the end. The total change to $V(s)$ is $\alpha \sum_t \delta_t z_t(s)$. Swap the order of summation:

$$\sum_{t} \delta_t\, z_t(s) = \sum_{k:\ S_k = s}\ \sum_{t \ge k} (\gamma\lambda)^{t-k} \delta_t = \sum_{k:\ S_k = s} \big(G^\lambda_k - V(S_k)\big)$$

The last step is Lesson 57's identity $G^\lambda_k - V(S_k) = \sum_{t \ge k} (\gamma\lambda)^{t-k} \delta_t$. So the backward view (traces) adds up to exactly the forward view (λ-returns). Updating online, as here, changes $V$ during the episode and makes the match approximate, close when $\alpha$ is small.

The cost is one extra number per state and an update of every state with a nonzero trace on each step. The gain is that credit from a reward reaches many past states at once, without waiting for the episode to end.
